notes: §1985:VII.4.6.4 GR2 "Within a declarative procedure, there must be no reference to any nondeclarative procedures"; a violating program is not conforming and §1985:I.1.6 leaves its result undefined ("The results of violating the formats or rules of Standard COBOL are undefined unless otherwise specified in this standard"), so WiseOwl's documented answer (docs/CONFORMANCE.md D-DECLREF) is warning COBOL2375. Every procedure-name operand funnels through ProcedureTableBuilder#ResolveProcedureOperand into StatementValidation#CheckDeclarativesBoundary, which warns on any reference from a declarative section to a nondeclarative procedure except RESUME; at --std 85 RESUME is refused outright (COBOL0876), so the 2023 exception cannot be reached. Probes at 85 (sequential file, USE after a failed OPEN/READ): PERFORM, PERFORM THRU (both ends), GO TO, GO TO DEPENDING (each operand), ALTER (both operands) each draw COBOL2375 and run as written; RESUME in a declarative is refused (COBOL0876); the witness exercises the legal form (only declarative references, USE runs, control returns after the READ). The warning text quotes the 2023 SR3 with its RESUME exception even at --std 85.

next.reason: 1985: "Within a declarative procedure, there must be no reference to any nondeclarative procedures."; 2023: "there shall be no reference to any nondeclarative procedures except in a RESUME statement.". Same prohibition, but 2023 adds a case: a declarative may refer to a nondeclarative procedure in a RESUME statement, which the 1985 rule forbids without exception.
